results.caption:
Death runs through The Sopranos from the first episode to the last. Chase has said the show was always, at its core, about mortality. Tony's panic attacks begin not because of his work, but because he feels time running out. The ducks leaving the pool in the pilot is the moment Chase said the whole series crystallized for him.

The dream sequences were not stylistic experiments. Chase used them as a way to access what Tony could not consciously admit. "The dream world is the real world," Chase said. "Everything Tony can't say out loud, he says there."

When asked in 2019 whether the finale's cut to black was a slip of the tongue when he called it a "death scene," Chase said: "No." Then in 2021 he confirmed: "Because the scene I had in my mind was not that scene. I had a scene in which Tony comes back from a meeting in New York in his car, and the last scene could be him coming from New Jersey back into New York for a meeting at which he was going to be killed."

What annoyed Chase most was not the ambiguity debate. It was the audience's desire to see Tony die. "They wanted to see him go face-down in linguini," he said. "You watched this guy for seven years. Don't tell me you're not on his side in some way. And now you want to see him killed. You're a criminal after watching this for seven years."

Series: The Sopranos (1999)

results.caption:
A HUGE cultural difference is our summer night hours here in the suburbs of Madrid, Spain. 

Every night this summer around 11:00pm/23:00, our doorbell rings. The urba kids are asking our kids to come out for the night! 😮 

Our 11 and 13-year olds will stay out there until midnight/00:00, running around and playing games in the streets of our urba. The kids range from 7-13 years old 😮

In the U.S., I would have never rang the doorbell of a neighbor after 9:00pm, even in summer. 

How would you do with this, American 🇺🇸 moms? I just head to bed now and they come in on their own, but Type A, scheduler and planning Meg a decade ago could never 🤣 

Cultural differences | summer in Spain | tres cantos | third culture kids

🇺🇸 🇪🇸: I’m Meg, a wife to my college sweetheart and mom to two bros (13 & 11!) and we’ve called Madrid home since 2023 besides spending six months by the Mediterranean Sea ♥️ I love to help other families consider a move to Spain, too, so on any post in 2026 comment MOVETOSPAIN and I’ll connect with you personally (no auto replies - it’s really me!). results.caption:
A South Brisbane road-rage incident has descended into a beautifully layered piece of Australian street theatre, after an opportunistic pedestrian abandoned his shopping trolley to have a crack at stealing an unattended vehicle.

The vehicle’s owner had stopped in the middle of the road moments earlier, to confront a man filming with his missus. The street documentarian responded by hiding behind his partner and letting him know: “It’s not worth it, mate.”

While everyone was distracted, a random bloke pushing a shopping trolley assessed the situation, abandoned the trolley in the middle of the road and attempted to upgrade his trolley to a car.

The owner of the car sprinted back, dragged the would-be thief out and drove away. Leaving Australians to determine the evening’s greatest offence: Jumping out of your running car for a cheeky bit of road rage, hiding behind your missus, or failing to return your shopping trolley?

results.caption: Easiest, longest, most boring zone one workout of my life  Finished well within the cut off times including my transitions 2.5 hours for the swim, 10.5 hours for the swim and bike and under 17 hours for everything. Took it slow and easy and just paced for 10-20 minutes before cutoff. Wish I hadn’t because the day was boringgggg.   I also bought bike shorts for this Absolutely no training. Never swam more than 100 yards. Never biked more than 5 miles (two days prior to see if it was possible) and yeah I’ve run a couple marathons but I have only run a handful of times this year.  When my buddy @Chris C challenged me to do it I thought there is no way I can’t do it because I have such a long time to. 17 hours is forever bro they got to make it shorter.  The only logistical way for me to get a run a bike and a swim in was to do it in and around my apartment complex.  I paced to do it as close to the time limits as possible. Definitely could’ve gone faster but didn’t want to burn out as I had never done it. Oh and I did a terrible job carb loading (I started the day before) which consisted of no breakfast, pancakes for lunch, pasta for dinner, and almost a gallon of apple juice. I got food poisoning somehow and threw up all night every last bit of the pasta. Didn’t sleep and was either freezing or super hot and in a pool of sweat. After I got up I was walking to the pool and had to run out to the front of the apartment to throw up all of the water I drank that morning and straight stomach acid. Still ripped it. You have no excuse it isn’t hard it is just really long and boring.  Oh and I was live on Instagram the whole day with the exception of the second half of the marathon so my phone didn’t die since it couldn’t be plugged in as I ran.  Thank you to everyone who tuned in! And a special thank you to Chris who pulled up to watch my marathon and @miguel_villaca who came and checked on me after my live went down and even got some miles in without running for years. Absolute legends . #ironman #ironmantraining #ironmantriathlon #fullironman
